summary: An independent reviewer (a separate AI model that never saw the tool's answers) checked all 54 bills from the raw records, and a person then confirmed every contested call. First pass: 46 of 54 agreed (85%). Of the 8 differences, 7 were rule errors we fixed and 1 we kept on purpose. The 2 misses we found ourselves were fixed before the review ran, so the very first version would have agreed on at most 44. After the fixes, 53 of 54 agree (98%), on the same bills the rules were fixed against, so that is not a fresh-data score: the shadow week measures that.

entries.why: Two months before this bill, the customer filed a complaint with the state consumer affairs office and threatened to contest the card charge over a 35% renewal increase. The tool only linked tickets raised after the bill.
entries.change: A chargeback, regulator or legal threat in the last 180 days stops chasing, whenever it was raised, until the account manager and Head of Support confirm it is settled.

entries.why: The customer opened chargebacks on two payments (2 July). The ticket was 121 days old and the first window was 120.
entries.change: Same rule, with a 180-day window as a setting.

entries.foundBy: Our own check, before the review (shown to Maya)
entries.why: The ticket named this invoice and refused to pay for a cancelled module, but the rules read "cancellation" as an escalation, not a dispute, so the tool said call.
entries.change: A ticket naming an unpaid bill is a dispute whatever else the rules call it; every call shows the customer's tickets beside it.

entries.foundBy: Our own check, before the review (shown to Maya)
entries.why: "Late fee should not be there": the word "outage" made it an escalation, so the dispute was missed. Saved only by the top-50 rule.
Only 4 days late. The policy's first reminder goes at 7 days.
entries.change: Bills under 7 days late wait; the first reminder comes back on day 7.

entries.why: The same customer also gets a call about an 83-day bill: an email and a call on the same day.
entries.change: One conversation per customer: other bills are covered on the same call.

entries.foundBy: Independent review, after a rule change
entries.why: Two days earlier the customer asked where a duplicate-charge refund Ledgerline had approved was. Zendesk marked it solved. Its pending product ticket had kept it on hold; when we stopped pending tickets blocking, it would have switched to a reminder to someone we owe money. The review caught it before any version went out.
entries.change: A money complaint from the last 30 days holds the bill even when Zendesk marks it solved.

entries.why: The "pending" ticket's last message from the customer was "Closing this out"; the word "wiped" in the subject made it look serious.
entries.change: When the customer says it's resolved, the ticket stops blocking.

entries.why: A normal-priority question "pending" since July: in Zendesk that means support is waiting on the customer.
entries.change: Decided with the team: a pending ticket blocks only if it's about money, high priority, or still waiting on Ledgerline. Otherwise a softer reminder, and the account manager is told.

entries.why: A pending timer bug, mis-tagged How-to. Not about money.
The reviewer would send: the open ticket is a product question, not a dispute. The tool holds because the ticket is open and waiting on Ledgerline (3 days).
entries.change: Kept on purpose: an open ticket waiting on us still pauses the reminder, and it's a top-50 account, so a person reads it either way.

entries.foundBy: Second look at the hand check
entries.why: One $5,100 payment with a blank memo and two $5,100 bills. The tool assumed it pays the older one, so the newer one would have got a reminder with no check. The reviewer's 'send' was conditional on that, and the hand check passed it. If the payment was for the newer bill, that's the Paidly case.
entries.change: When a payment could cover either of two same-amount bills, both go to Check first and Marcus confirms which before any reminder.

entries.why: Customers also reply to billing@ in Gmail. Disputes sent there are invisible to the tool and aren't in the data room.
entries.change: Next step: read the billing@ inbox (Google is already a vendor).
